question: A 54-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of fever, chills, and double vision. She also has a 2-week history of headache and foul-smelling nasal discharge. Her temperature is 39.4°C (103°F). Examination shows mild swelling around the left eye. Her left eye does not move past midline on far left gaze but moves normally when looking to the right. Without treatment, which of the following findings is most likely to occur in this patient?
analysis: The patient's presentation is consistent with cavernous sinus thrombosis, likely secondary to sinusitis. The left eye not moving past midline on far left gaze suggests involvement of the sixth cranial nerve (abducens nerve). Without treatment, the most likely finding to occur in this patient would be jaw deviation due to involvement of the trigeminal nerve (cranial nerve V).
